My job means that a lot of my recipes end up as burritos (easier to throw down range while driving down the road) and the macros aren't quite there if you do IIFYM but here goes my veggie burritos.

Ingredients

  • 1 container of hummus
  • 1 cup uncooked rice
  • 2 portobello caps
  • 2 red bell peppers
  • 2 green bell peppers
  • 2 yellow bell peppers
  • 8 burrito tortillas
  • Hot skillet
  • Mixing bowl
  • Aluminum foil
  • Optional: Small measure of olive oil for the skillet.
  • Optional: I put salad greens in just about everything.

Directions

  1. Set the rice to cook
  2. Dice the portobello and all the peppers. Set them in the hot skillet.
  3. Empty the hummus and greens into the mix bowl.
  4. Add the cooked mushroom and pepper mix to the bowl.
  5. Add the cooked rice to the mix bowl.
  6. Portion the filling evenly into the tortilla wraps.
  7. Wrap the burrito and cover in foil.

Reheat instructions

300F for 30 minutes does the trick for me, but these are tasty hot or cold.

Nutrition per Burrito

  • Calories: 529
  • Fat: 22.5
  • Carbs: 63.4
  • Protein: 19.4

“This is really good for large business, especially big companies. They can hire cheaper foreign labor, often under the books, to do jobs that it would cost more for a German to do. “This is not good for us, the workers. Especially not us trade unionists. We don’t care about some perceived ‘labor shortage’; we want German jobs to go to Germans, and that’s that.

“Thus, after conferring that I was far from alone in my feelings, that most all of my coworkers are coming to see this as my way, I think I can speak for all of us little guys when I say that I don’t want want to have my livelihood threatened by cheap foreign labor. I could go on, but in short: we, the workers, have no love for immigrants. And we like very much not to deal with them.

“Most of us Unionists have voted SPD, since up until recently, you were with us. But I’ll tell you this, Herr Rosenthal, you’ll not have my vote a second time. If given the chance, he’d overrun us with cheap labor and drive us all out in the name of ‘diversity’, ‘humanity’, and ‘multiculturalism’ and other buzzwords that big business likes to use to explain why they want cheaper slave labor to hard-working German nationals. “I’m here to take a stands for my friends, family, and coworkers; come what way unto me in retribution for speaking out against the status quo.

“Sincerely,

“An Everyday German Worker.”
